vendors.name: Kahuku Mango Bros

vendors.description: ʻAhi, aku

vendors.name: Cindy's Lei Shoppe
vendors.description: Pīkake, maile, plumeria and haku lei, made to order
vendors.story: A family business on Maunakea Street since 1959, and the Star-Advertiser readers' pick for best lei stand in twelve of the last thirteen years.
vendors.good_to_know: Curbside pickup: call when you reach Maunakea and Beretania and they bring the order out to the car. Ships fresh lei to all fifty states.

vendors.name: Pauahi Leis
vendors.story: A small shop run by Lilia and her daughter Lenny.
vendors.good_to_know: On Pauahi Street. The exact address and phone number are not confirmed.

vendors.name: Maunakea Florist
vendors.good_to_know: On Maunakea Street. The exact address and phone number are not confirmed.

vendors.name: Harriet's Lei Stand
vendors.description: Fresh flower lei at the airport lei stands
vendors.good_to_know: Stall 1 on the airport lei road, before Terminal 1. The state airports page lists the lei stands as generally open 6a to 10p; this stand does not post its own hours.

vendors.name: Rachel's Lei Stand
vendors.description: Fresh flower lei and arrangements
vendors.story: Family owned and run for more than ninety years, per the Native Hawaiian Business Directory.
vendors.good_to_know: On the airport lei road; the stall number is not confirmed. The state airports page lists the lei stands as generally open 6a to 10p.

vendors.name: Dorothy's Lei Stand
vendors.good_to_know: On the airport lei road; the stall number is not confirmed. The state airports page lists the lei stands as generally open 6a to 10p.

vendors.name: Gladys' Lei Stand
vendors.story: Opened by Moana Umi, whose mother Rachel Aanana sold lei on the waterfront and on Maunakea Street. The family stand has been on Lagoon Drive since 1948.
vendors.good_to_know: On the airport lei road; the stall number is not confirmed. The state airports page lists the lei stands as generally open 6a to 10p.

vendors.name: Maile's Lei Stand
vendors.story: A family lei stand since 1945, when it worked out of a truck on Lagoon Drive. It took the name Maile's in 1962, when Maile Lee inherited it.
vendors.good_to_know: On the airport lei road; the stall number is not confirmed. The state airports page lists the lei stands as generally open 6a to 10p.

vendors.name: Watanabe Floral
vendors.description: Florist with a lei department, island-wide delivery
vendors.story: A full-service florist with its own lei department, taking orders online and delivering island-wide.
vendors.good_to_know: On Nimitz between Kalihi Street and Waikamilo Road.

vendors.name: Lin's Lei Shop
vendors.description: Fresh flower lei made to order, plus arrangements and wedding bouquets
vendors.story: A family owned and operated shop on Maunakea Street, voted best lei stand in the 2017 and 2018 Best of hiChinatown awards.
vendors.good_to_know: Their own website is offline, so the list of what they make comes from an archived copy of it from January 2021 and may have changed. The hours come from their hiChinatown listing.

vendors.name: Nico's Pier 38 Fish Market
vendors.description: Auction-fresh fillets, poke and smoked seafood
vendors.story: Founded by chef Nico Chaize next door to the Honolulu Fish Auction, which is where the fish counter buys each morning.
vendors.good_to_know: The sit-down restaurant at the same address is a separate operation with its own phone and later hours; this listing is the retail fish market. Prepared-food counters inside the market keep shorter hours than the market itself.

vendors.name: Pier 38 Fish Market
vendors.description: Fresh fillets, sashimi platters and poke kits
vendors.story: The retail arm of Fresh Island Fish Co., a wholesale distributor since 1977 sourcing from the Hawaii Longline Association. It says it is Hawaiʻi's first and only MSC-certified fish market, and sold wholesale only until the pandemic.
vendors.good_to_know: Two fish markets sit side by side at Pier 38; Nico's next door at 1129 is a different business. Online orders for local pickup at shop.pier38fishmarket.com.

vendors.name: Alicia's Market
vendors.description: Kalihi corner market with a poke case about 18 varieties deep
vendors.story: Founded in 1949 by Alicia and Raymond Kam and now run by their grandsons Chris and Brad. A 2018 fire destroyed the kitchen; the store reopened in the rebuilt original location in late 2022.
vendors.good_to_know: Hours are as reported by Honolulu Magazine; the store's own site does not post them.

vendors.name: Poke by the Pound
vendors.description: Poke and sashimi by the pound
vendors.good_to_know: The shop says all its fish is sourced locally and never frozen.

vendors.name: Honolulu Fish Company
vendors.description: Sashimi-grade fish shipped overnight anywhere in the US
vendors.story: Founded in 1995 by marine biologist Wayne Samiere, buying hand-selected fish at the Honolulu Fish Auction each morning. No net-caught fish and no immature fish.
vendors.good_to_know: Primarily an online and wholesale business; whether walk-in retail exists at Gulick Avenue is not stated anywhere, so call before visiting. Consumer orders at honolulufishmarket.com ship overnight in a cold-chain box.

vendors.name: Maguro Brothers Hawaii
vendors.description: Sashimi and poke bowls from the morning fish auction
vendors.story: Run by brothers Junichiro and Ryojiro Tsuchiya, who opened in Kekaulike Market in 2014 and later moved to Maunakea Marketplace. The fish is bought directly from the Honolulu fish auction.
vendors.good_to_know: Inside Maunakea Marketplace. Sells bowls, cups and platters rather than fillets by the pound; custom sashimi platters can be preordered online.

vendors.name: Maguro Brothers Hawaii Waikīkī
vendors.description: Evening sashimi and poke bowls
vendors.story: The evening location of the Chinatown stand, opened in 2016 and later moved to Kalākaua Avenue.
vendors.good_to_know: Open evenings only. Same auction-sourced fish as the Chinatown location.

vendors.name: Morning Catch
vendors.description: Poke by the pound inside Oʻahu Market
vendors.story: Opened in March 2021 inside Oʻahu Market, with fish from the 88 Fresh Fish stall next door, sauced to order.
vendors.good_to_know: Hours are as reported by Honolulu Magazine in 2024. A second counter in Kekaulike Market facing Hotel Street opened in 2023.

vendors.name: 88 Fresh Fish
vendors.description: Fresh whole fish daily inside Oʻahu Market
vendors.good_to_know: Hours are as listed in the Slow Food Oʻahu guide. Cleaning and filleting are free. Supplies the Morning Catch poke counter next door.

vendors.name: Blue Seafood Company
vendors.description: Daily-changing fresh fish and poke in Maunakea Marketplace
vendors.story: Opened in February 2025 with a fresh fish counter and a food-court stall that will cook your purchase.
vendors.good_to_know: Published sources conflict on both the phone number and the exact hours, so neither is listed here; the market side has been reported open roughly 7a to 3:30p daily.

vendors.name: Yama's Fish Market
vendors.description: Poke and Hawaiian food, takeout only
vendors.story: Family-run since 1980, growing from a neighborhood fish market into a Hawaiian food institution. The ʻahi comes from the daily Honolulu fish auction and the limu poke is the signature.
vendors.good_to_know: Takeout only, no seating, with seven parking stalls on site. The site posts a full holiday-hours schedule each year.

vendors.name: Ono Seafood
vendors.description: Made-to-order poke by the pound
vendors.story: The Kapahulu original opened in 2006; a second location followed in Kalama Valley in 2019.
vendors.good_to_know: No working website; the old domain is parked and several lookalike sites are unofficial. Posted hours could not be confirmed from a current source, so call ahead.

vendors.name: Fresh Catch
vendors.description: Poke, sashimi platters and plate lunches
vendors.story: Chef and owner Reno Henriques buys off the Honolulu auction block. First place in Hawaiʻi's Best 2023.
vendors.good_to_know: Takeout deli format, not a sit-down restaurant. A Sand Island food truck also runs Fridays 10a to 1p.

vendors.name: Fresh Catch Kāneʻohe
vendors.description: Poke, sashimi platters and plate lunches, windward side
vendors.story: The windward location of Fresh Catch, Chef Reno Henriques' takeout seafood deli.
vendors.good_to_know: Closes an hour later than the Kapahulu shop on Tuesday through Saturday.

vendors.name: Off the Hook Poke Market
vendors.description: ʻAhi poke by the pound from the daily auction
vendors.story: Opened in 2018; its Cold Ginger ʻAhi with ginger scallion sauce is the signature. All ʻahi comes fresh from the Honolulu Fish Auction daily.

vendors.name: Tamura's Fine Wine & Liquors Waiʻalae
vendors.description: Poke bar inside the wine shop
vendors.story: Four generations of the Tamura family; the wine shops date to 1995 and every location runs a poke bar made fresh daily.
vendors.good_to_know: Takeout only; the poke can sell out by afternoon.

vendors.name: Tamura's Fine Wine & Liquors Pearlridge
vendors.description: Poke bar inside the wine shop
vendors.good_to_know: Takeout only; the poke can sell out by afternoon.

vendors.name: Tamura's Fine Wine & Liquors Aikahi
vendors.description: Poke bar inside the wine shop
vendors.good_to_know: Takeout only; the poke can sell out by afternoon.

vendors.name: K.Bay Bros Fish & Ice
vendors.description: 20-plus poke varieties daily, plus bagged ice
vendors.story: Opened in September 2021 across from Windward Mall by the four Koki brothers, who grew up fishing off Heʻeia. The name honors Kāneʻohe Bay.
vendors.good_to_know: The fish is a mix of fresh and frozen from local fishermen and suppliers. Posted hours could not be confirmed from a current source, so check before driving over.

vendors.name: Kahuku Superette
vendors.description: Famous poke counter at the back of a country store
vendors.story: A plain convenience store with a poke counter that made it a required stop on round-island drives. The shoyu poke is the signature.
vendors.good_to_know: Published sources conflict on the hours and the store posts none online, so call ahead.

vendors.name: Tanioka's Seafoods & Catering
vendors.description: Poke, sashimi and okazuya since 1978
vendors.story: Founded in 1978 by Mel and Lynn Tanioka, growing from one rented retail stall into its own building. Their children Jasmine and Justin run it today.
vendors.good_to_know: Online ordering for pickup. Merchandise ships to the mainland but the food does not.

vendors.name: Waiʻanae Store
vendors.description: Supermarket with fresh poke on the Waiʻanae coast
vendors.story: A family-owned supermarket since 1949, operated by Okimoto Corp, and the largest food store on the coast between Kapolei and Mākaha.
vendors.good_to_know: The store advertises fresh poke and a meat and fish counter but does not list fish types.

vendors.name: Local Iʻa
vendors.description: Community supported fishery with weekly island fish shares
vendors.story: Hawaiʻi's first community supported fishery, built around loko iʻa and supporting lawaiʻa who fish with pono practices. Fish is island-local, line- or spear-caught and sashimi-grade.
vendors.good_to_know: Retail hours are as listed in the Slow Food Oʻahu guide; the Kaimukī outlet opens Friday and Saturday only, and a Sunday morning stand runs at the Mililani Farmers Market. Weekly CSF shares pick up at locations across the island.

markets.name: Kaimukī Neighborhood Market
markets.description: Mon, Wed and Sat mornings behind the community center on Koko Head Ave. 14 vendors today, mostly produce and poi. Small lot, easier to park on the side street.
markets.location_notes: Koko Head Ave, behind the community center
markets.getting_there: Lot fills by 7a. Route 9 stops one block makai. Bring your own bags and small bills.
